target_moa.text: Abemaciclib is a kinase inhibitor with activity against cyclin-dependent kinase 4 (CDK4) and CDK6; CDK4/6 in complex with D-type cyclins phosphorylate Rb protein, and inhibition leads to G1 cell cycle arrest in Rb-positive breast cancer cells.

citations.quote: Abemaciclib is a kinase inhibitor with activity against cyclin-dependent kinase 4 (CDK4) and CDK6. CDKs regulate cell cycle entry and commitment to cell division. CDK4 and CDK6 in complex with D-type cyclins (CycD) control progression from G1 to S phase of the cell cycle.
Abemaciclib exposure for up to four days inhibited Rb phosphorylation (IC_{50} = 12-67 nM) and DNA synthesis (IC_{50} = 178 nM) and caused G1 cell cycle arrest
Abemaciclib is a weakly basic, small molecule (MW: 506.6 g/mol) which reversibly inhibits cyclin-dependent kinase 4 (CDK4) and cyclin-dependent kinase 6 (CDK6)

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=20%) were diarrhea, neutropenia, nausea, abdominal pain, infections, fatigue, anemia, leukopenia, decreased appetite, vomiting, headache, and thrombocytopenia. In MONARCH 2, diarrhea occurred in 86% (vs 25% placebo), neutropenia 46% (vs 4%), and fatigue 46% (vs 32%). Serious risks include neutropenia (2 deaths from neutropenic sepsis), hepatotoxicity, and venous thromboembolism.

summary.text: Abemaciclib received Breakthrough Therapy Designation (Oct 2015) and Fast Track Designation (Nov 2015), and the NDA was granted Priority Review. It was approved during the first cycle without an advisory committee meeting or accelerated approval; approval was based on the Phase 3 MONARCH 2 PFS result and the single-arm Phase 2 MONARCH 1 ORR result.
